designSummary: Random-effects meta-analysis of log odds ratios for haemolysis, randomised and non-randomised studies analysed separately, with pre-specified subgroup analyses and meta-regression.
sampleSize: The prior review found 24 studies to 2022; with later studies about 30 to 35 are expected. Subgroup analysis and meta-regression are planned only for effect modifiers with at least ten studies, because with I-squared near 88 percent fewer studies give unstable estimates. A 95 percent prediction interval is reported alongside every pooled estimate so that the likely range in a new setting is visible.
primaryAnalysis: Random-effects model (restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment) for the odds ratio of haemolysis with catheter draws versus venepuncture, separately for randomised and non-randomised comparisons.
secondaryAnalysis: Subgroups by tube type or syringe, catheter gauge, collector training and transport; meta-regression on the proportion of low-vacuum draws if at least ten studies report it; sensitivity analysis restricted to analyser index definitions; descriptive paediatric results.
missingData: Authors are not contacted within the available hours; studies without extractable counts are described narratively and counted in the flow diagram.
multiplicity: One primary estimate per design group; subgroup findings are reported as hypothesis-generating with an interaction test.
overfittingGuards: Effect modifiers limited to four, fixed in the registered protocol
Meta-regression only with ten or more studies
Prediction intervals reported with every pooled estimate
summary: About 30 to 35 studies expected; subgroups only with ten or more studies; prediction intervals throughout.
